questions.stem: Aluminium is extracted by electrolysis, while iron is extracted by reduction with carbon in a blast furnace. What determines which method is used?

options.text: The cost of each method determines the choice
Aluminium is above carbon in the reactivity series, so carbon cannot reduce it
Iron ores are more common than aluminium ores
Electrolysis only works for metals that are shiny

questions.explanation: The extraction method depends on the metal's position in the reactivity series relative to carbon. Metals below carbon (like iron, zinc, lead) can be extracted by reduction with carbon. Metals above carbon (like aluminium, sodium, calcium) are too reactive and must be extracted by electrolysis, which is more expensive.

questions.stem: A mining company discovers an ore containing copper oxide. What is the most cost-effective method to extract copper from this ore?

options.text: Electrolysis, because it produces the purest copper
Heating with carbon, because copper is below carbon in the reactivity series
Reacting with water, because copper dissolves in water
No extraction is needed; copper is found as a native element

questions.explanation: Copper is below carbon in the reactivity series, so copper oxide can be reduced by heating with carbon: CuO + C -> Cu + CO2. This is cheaper than electrolysis. While copper can sometimes be found native, copper oxide is a compound that requires extraction. Electrolysis can purify copper further but is more expensive for initial extraction.

questions.stem: Why is recycling aluminium cans much more beneficial than recycling iron cans from an energy perspective?

options.text: Aluminium is rarer than iron so it costs more to buy
Extracting aluminium by electrolysis uses vastly more energy than reducing iron with carbon
Aluminium cans are lighter so they are easier to transport
Iron cannot be recycled but aluminium can

questions.explanation: Extracting aluminium from its ore requires electrolysis, which uses enormous amounts of electrical energy. Recycling aluminium saves up to 95% of this energy. While iron extraction also uses energy, the blast furnace process is already less energy-intensive than electrolysis. Both metals can be recycled, but the energy saving is proportionally much greater for aluminium.

questions.stem: Gold and platinum are sometimes found as pure metals in the Earth's crust, but sodium and potassium are never found uncombined. Why is this?

options.text: Gold and platinum are too heavy to react with anything
Sodium and potassium are gases, so they escape from the ground
Gold and platinum are very unreactive and do not combine with other elements easily
Sodium and potassium are too rare to be found as pure metals

questions.explanation: Very unreactive metals (at the bottom of the reactivity series) like gold and platinum resist reacting with oxygen, water, and other substances, so they exist as native (pure) metals. Very reactive metals like sodium and potassium are at the top of the reactivity series and react readily with oxygen and water, so they are always found as compounds in ores.

questions.stem: Titanium is a very useful metal but is more reactive than carbon. However, it cannot be extracted by electrolysis of its molten chloride because it reacts with the carbon electrodes. How is titanium extracted instead?

options.text: By heating titanium chloride with a very reactive metal like sodium or magnesium
By dissolving it in acid and filtering
By heating titanium ore in a blast furnace with coke
It cannot be extracted and must be synthesised from other elements

questions.explanation: Titanium is extracted by displacing it from titanium chloride using a more reactive metal (sodium or magnesium) in the Kroll process: TiCl4 + 4Na -> Ti + 4NaCl. This works because sodium and magnesium are more reactive than titanium. Carbon reduction does not work because titanium is above carbon in reactivity, and the special electrolysis challenges require an alternative approach.
